gates.description: Service Level Objectives must be defined (availability, latency, error rate)
Error budget policy must be defined with organizational buy-in
On-call runbooks must exist for all alerts
Alerts must be on symptoms (user impact) not causes (high CPU)
Blameless postmortem process must be documented
Circuit breakers and graceful degradation must be defined

anti_patterns.description: Hundreds of alerts, most ignored — on-call engineer is desensitized
The same engineer saves the day every time — team celebrates hero instead of fixing system
Freezing deployments to prevent outages — nothing changes, nothing improves
Someone watches dashboards and manually scales services when traffic increases
We've always done it this way — manual processes become accepted without automation

escalation_triggers: Error budget exhausted with no clear path to recovery
Cascading failure affecting multiple services simultaneously
Capacity limits approaching and scaling is blocked
Recurring incidents with same root cause requiring architectural change
On-call burden unsustainable (>5 pages per shift consistently)

output_certifications: SLOs defined (availability, latency, error rate minimum)
Error budget policy defined with organizational buy-in
Runbooks written for all defined alerts
Alerting configured on SLO burn rate (symptoms not causes)
Graceful degradation and circuit breakers defined for all dependencies
